title: Enterprise Feature Request Carrier Map & Rapid Scope Accelerator
creator: Rina Kapoor
description:
Problem: CS and Sales surface a high volume of enterprise feature requests (non-bug) that often lack a consistent framing for product/engineering decisions. Current ad-hoc triage means long turnaround for a scoped response and extra context-gathering rounds that slow sales cycles.

Proposal: Build a repeatable 'Carrier Map' taxonomy + a Rapid Scope Accelerator play that enables CS+PM to produce a defensible 1-2 paragraph scope + effort band and next-step recommendation within 48 hours of intake. The Carrier Map groups incoming asks into solution carriers (eg. routing/pinning/fallbacks, observability dashboards, RBAC and audit, autoscaling policies, private deployment controls) with typical success patterns and effort heuristics. The Rapid Scope Accelerator is a compact checklist, templated write-up, and quick-engineering feasibility pass used for initial scoping.

Why this matters: faster, more consistent scoping will improve CS SLA to customers, shorten negotiation cycles for Dedicated/Private deals, and reduce PM context-switching.

Intended scope for pilot: 6-week pilot with Sales (AM teams) + CS Solutions to validate Carrier Map coverage across top enterprise asks and validate the 48-hour first-scope SLA for >80% of pilot tickets.

Deliverables:
- Carrier Map taxonomy doc and searchable index
- Rapid Scope template (consequence/benefit/approx effort/risks/first-next steps)
- Intake form tweak for Sales portal + Linear ticket template
- 1-week handbook + training session for CS on running the rapid scope exercise
- Pilot measurement dashboard in Looker with time-to-first-scope and conversion KPIs
acceptance_criteria: Carrier Map doc published in Confluence with at least 10 mapped carriers and sample resolved tickets
Rapid Scope template stored in Drive and linked from Linear ticket template
CS trained (one 45-minute workshop) and pilot kickoff with at least 3 AMs and 2 Solutions Engineers
Pilot covers 20 real enterprise requests and meets 48-hour first-scope SLA for >=80%
A baseline Looker report is available tracking time-to-first-scope and pilot conversion to committed work
success_metrics: Median time-to-first-scope reduced from current baseline to <=48 hours for pilot cohort
% of pilot tickets that require >2 follow-up context rounds reduced by 50%
Sales win pipeline influenced by scoped asks increases (tracked as $ value) — conversion target +10% over baseline within 90 days
PM time spent per intake reduced by 30% (measured via weekly time-tracking sample)
initial_scoping_notes:
Observed incoming asks fall into repeatable buckets: model routing/custom fallback, dedicated capacity config, VPC/auth controls, audit/log shipping, console dashboards for cost allocation, and per-route QoS. For each carrier we propose a typical effort band (tiny: 1-2 sprints; medium: 3-6 sprints; large: >6 sprints) and a technical-likelihood score based on dependencies (runtime, infra, compliance).

Example sample scope for 'per-route cost breakdown dashboard' (generated by pilot):
- Customer need: visible token-level cost per route and per-team
- Benefit: reduces disputes in enterprise billing and speeds procurement
- Rough effort band: medium (3 sprints across console + billing infra)
- Risks/deps: billing infra hooks, trace sampling, IAM perms
- Next step: engineer feasibility sync (30 min) + sample schema request
proposed_triage_rubric: Dependency count and cross-team coordination complexity
Revenue/time-to-value (how fast will it convert to committed spend)
Alternative workarounds (can CS provide a config or runbook in the interim)
